subject: biology
title: Organism
summary: An organism is any living thing - a plant, animal, fungus, or microbe - that can carry out the activities of life on its own. Explore what makes something alive and how a single organism fits into the natural world.

crossReferences.note: A group of the same kind of organism in one place is a population - the next level up.

crossReferences.label: Ecosystem (Ecology)

compareCandidate.label: Living vs. nonliving
compareCandidate.description: A rock or a car is nonliving: it does not grow, use energy, respond, or reproduce. A tree or a bacterium is living - it does all of these. Viruses are a tricky in-between case, since they need a host cell.

processes: Carrying out the activities of life
plainLanguageExplanation: An organism is any living thing: an oak tree, a dog, a mushroom, a bacterium. Every organism is made of cells and can carry out life activities - it grows, uses energy, responds to its surroundings, makes copies of itself (reproduces), and keeps its inside balanced. Organisms come in every size, from a single microscopic cell to a blue whale. Each organism is one living individual, and together individuals form populations, communities, and ecosystems.

keyFacts.label: Definition
keyFacts.value: Any living thing that can carry out the activities of life

keyFacts.label: Made of
keyFacts.value: All organisms are made of cells (one or many)

keyFacts.label: Activities
keyFacts.value: Grows, uses energy, responds, reproduces, stays balanced

keyFacts.label: Sizes
keyFacts.value: From a single bacterium to a giant blue whale

keyFacts.label: Level
keyFacts.value: The first level in the ecological hierarchy: organism -> population -> community -> ecosystem

whyItMatters: Organisms are the living units of the natural world - every ecosystem is built from them. Understanding what counts as an organism (and what makes something alive) is the foundation of all ecology.
didYouKnow: Your own body is an organism made of about 30 trillion cells working together.
